book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: A game with soldiers beginning to tire defender

parts.note: taken as written
polo is a game played on horseback
GIs are American soldiers

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of tire

explanation.surface: A soldier plays a game until fatigue begins to beat the defender on the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's 'Sw.' is a misreading of 'A', which the wordplay needs. 'Defender' looks like a sporting position but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in support of a cause or belief, so is its defender in debate.

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the idea that an opinion poll is the benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' looks like a vote but is the traditional pet name for a parrot, as in Polly.
explanation.definitionFit: Poll, short for Polly, is the conventional name for a pet parrot, so it stands for the bird.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a surgeon's pointed blade
second meaning: The ..., the British medical journal

explanation.surface: A knife turns up inside a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' suggests a hidden word, but it simply links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical blade and the famous weekly medical journal share the same name, which the journal took from the blade.

clue.text: Pass outside right, a person searching in the dark?

indicators.note: one thing being outside another means it wraps round it

parts.note: time goes, or passes
R is the abbreviation for right
per means a, as in so much a day

explanation.surface: A footballer passes from the outside-right position to someone fumbling about blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside right' is an old football position, but here outside is the container signal. The question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone feeling their way in darkness gropes about, so a groper is one who does that.

clue.text: Captain is one who plays with rope

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the master of a ship or leader of a team
second meaning: someone who jumps over a turning rope

explanation.walkthrough: A captain playing with rope sounds nautical, but the second meaning is a child jumping a skipping rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a ship's master or team leader, and literally a person who uses a skipping rope.

clue.text: Arrives at old entrance and departs it is assumed

parts.note: arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives
O is the abbreviation for old
a gate is a way in
d. is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A train timetable notes arrival at an old gate and departure from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrives and departs are both shortened as on a railway timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate a right is to assume or claim it without justification.

clue.text: Hardline broadcast about Nationalist in German region

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece
broadcast means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: An uncompromising nationalist programme is aired in a part of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardline broadcast' reads like hardline propaganda; it is the letters of hardline spread around the N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhineland is the region of western Germany along the river Rhine.

clue.text: German dish, hot with no end of spice

indicators.note: having no end of something means that letter is dropped, and hot comes in to take its place

parts.note: fried rice is a Chinese dish
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the end of spice is its final letter

explanation.surface: A spicy German meal, served hot with plenty of seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German dish' looks like one phrase; German alone is the definition, a German man's name. In the dish, H replaces the final letter of spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich is a typical German given name, borne by kings of Prussia, so it can stand for a German.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a soldier fighting with bow and arrows
second meaning: comparative of arch, meaning sly or knowing

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is'. Arch as an adjective means slyly knowing, so its comparative is a second sense of the bowman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowmen were the long-range soldiers of ancient armies, and arch means roguishly sly, with a comparative form in -er.

clue.text: Partridge old dictator left at home

parts.note: General Franco ruled Spain until 1975
L is the standard abbreviation for left
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A partridge watches the elderly despot who has stayed behind in his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partridge' could suggest the comedy character Alan Partridge, but here it is the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The francolin is a game bird of Africa and Asia belonging to the partridge family.

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A black cat appears in the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes 'Spring' look like the season; it is the verb or noun for a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce is to rebound or leap up, and a spring is a jump of exactly that kind.

clue.text: PM is of assistance to domestic staff

parts.note: Sir Alec Douglas-Home was British Prime Minister in 1963-64
to be of assistance is to help

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister lends a hand to the household servants.
explanation.walkthrough: PM stands for Prime Minister; the crossword trick is to think of one specific holder of the office, Douglas-Home.
explanation.definitionFit: Home helps are people employed, often by a local council in Britain, to do housework for those who need it.

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A clothes-maker sets off in pursuit of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor makes and sells clothes, which is what a clothier does.

parts.note: to off something is slang for doing away with it
a raspberry is a rude noise of derision, like a hoot

explanation.surface: Someone prunes the canes from the fruit bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raspberries' sounds like the fruit, which suits the branches, but it means jeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Offshoots are side stems growing from a main stem, which is what branches are.

parts.note: asses are fools
to sing or squeal is slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: Scheming fools blab to the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calculating' wants to mean scheming, to go with the informers, but it is the definition in its sense of working out.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessing a sum or value means estimating it, a form of calculating.

clue.text: They never describe themselves as such

definitions.text: They never describe themselves as such

parts.words: They never describe themselves as such
parts.note: surface reading: some group too modest to use their own label

parts.words: They never describe themselves as such
parts.note: setter's reading: the old idea that a man of real breeding would never claim that title for himself

explanation.walkthrough: The clue rests on an old maxim of good manners: claiming the title is itself proof you do not deserve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional etiquette held that a true man of breeding would never boast of his status, so such men never apply the word to themselves.

clue.text: Wood-nymph lacking notice is far from sweet

indicators.note: something lacking a part has had it taken away

parts.note: a dryad is a tree spirit of Greek myth
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A nymph of the woods, ignored by everyone, turns sour.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the notice from the end of the nymph leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry wine has little residual sugar, so it is the opposite of sweet.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Delaware
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A colour nobody can identify in Delaware.
explanation.definitionFit: A dye is a substance used to colour things, and to colour is to dye.

clue.text: Anyone getting eulogy regularly on retirement

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the letters run the opposite way
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of eulogy

explanation.surface: Every retiree gets a tribute speech now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: The generic 'you' means one or anyone, as in 'you never know'.

clue.text: Right of queen to enter dubious environment

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within another
an environment is the surroundings, so the dubious word encloses what enters

parts.note: something fishy is suspect
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A queen's prerogative to move into a shady setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right of queen' reads as a royal prerogative, but 'Right' alone is the definition, in its legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a fishery can mean the right to catch fish in particular waters, as well as the place itself.

indicators.note: to manufacture is to make something new out of raw material, so the letters are made into a fresh word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Producing cocaine, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the high seas, so something in the main is at sea, relating to the ocean.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the large flightless Australian bird
second meaning: the electromagnetic unit used in physics

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is'. The physics sense is the abbreviation for electromagnetic unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a big Australian ratite and the old electromagnetic unit of physics.

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece goes second

parts.note: a mate is a spouse
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: A seaman's fate is to go where his wife leads.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang, from French, for a sailor.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a heath is open moorland

explanation.surface: Taking shelter out on a moor in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' might suggest mooring a boat; here it is the open land.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting case that covers a blade or similar object.

parts.note: surface reading: a creature with a sharp spike or snout
setter's reading: the creature's name is shared with a headland, the most southerly point of mainland Britain, in Cornwall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' suggests a sharp tip, but it means a promontory: the Lizard Point is the southern tip of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaly reptile shares its name with the Lizard, the Cornish peninsula ending at Lizard Point.

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a cod is a fish
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fish swims up to the surface to take a titbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat' looks like a reward for the fish but is the verb meaning to give medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor a patient is to give them medical treatment.

clue.text: One applying pressure has to move fast with strength

parts.note: to steam along is to travel at speed
iron stands for firmness and strength, as in an iron will

explanation.surface: A forceful person must rush around showing their power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One applying pressure' suggests a bully or campaigner; it is the household appliance pressed onto clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron presses creases out of fabric, so it literally applies pressure.

indicators.note: fabricating means making up, so the letters are put together in a new form

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps quiet is caught inventing a tale about England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-lipped person is called an oyster because the shellfish stays firmly shut.

clue.text: Prospectors, perhaps, in Sri Lanka to target insects

parts.note: CL is Sri Lanka's international vehicle code, from its old name Ceylon
to target is to aim at
ants are insects

explanation.surface: Gold-seekers in Sri Lanka go after the local bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospectors stake claims to land, so they are an example of people making claims.

clue.text: Apply metal to most of edge in poor repair

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but the final letter

parts.note: to tin is to coat with the metal tin
a kerb is the edge of a pavement (curb in the US)

explanation.surface: Plating the rim of something that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The kerb loses its last letter before joining the metal coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinker, as a noun, is an amateurish attempt to mend something, a fiddle rather than a real fix.

parts.note: taken as written
tenders are formal offers or bids

explanation.surface: The witnesses when marriage proposals are made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proposals' brings marriage to mind, but these are business bids.
explanation.definitionFit: Attenders are the people who turn up at an event, so they are the ones present.
